translation: Machine translation (Claude, 5 Nov 2026) of the reviewed Indonesian file next to it; needs owner review. Same ids, option order and correct answers as the Indonesian source (decision 0185).
schemaNote: mc follows decision 0013 (correct + wrong[3]); every quote is verbatim from its sourceChunk in assets/module/module_chunks.json

items.question: Food scraps and dry leaves break down naturally. What is true about the material this waste comes from?
items.correct: It comes from living things and is broken down naturally by microorganisms
wrong: It comes from synthetic materials and is very hard for microorganisms to break down
It contains hazardous and toxic materials, so it must be kept in a special container
It comes from mineral materials and can stay in the environment for hundreds of years
items.explanation: The module defines organic waste as waste from animals and plants that microorganisms break down naturally.
items.quote: Sampah organik adalah sampah yang berasal dari makhluk hidup (hewan dan tumbuhan) dan dapat terurai secara alami oleh mikroorganisme dalam jangka waktu tertentu.

items.question: What is the property of organic waste that can be broken down biologically called?
items.correct: Biodegradable
wrong: Non-biodegradable
Corrosive
Reactive
items.explanation: The module calls being biologically degradable 'biodegradable'; corrosive and reactive are B3 characteristics.
items.quote: Sifat ini disebut biodegradable, yaitu dapat diuraikan secara biologis (Damanhuri dan Padmi, 2010).

items.question: Why can aerobic composting help kill pathogens and weed seeds?
items.correct: Because the process produces heat of 50-70°C
wrong: Because the process happens without oxygen
Because the process produces methane gas that kills germs
Because the process uses earthworms that eat weed seeds
items.explanation: Aerobic composting uses microorganisms that need oxygen and produces heat of 50-70°C, which helps kill pathogens.
items.quote: Prosesnya lebih cepat dan menghasilkan panas 50-70°C yang membantu membunuh patogen (kuman penyakit) dan biji gulma.

items.question: Which process produces biogas from organic waste?
items.correct: Anaerobic fermentation of organic matter by methanogenic bacteria
wrong: Aerobic composting with a pile that is turned regularly
Breakdown by earthworms in a vermicompost box
Open burning of organic waste at the landfill
items.explanation: The module explains that biogas comes from anaerobic fermentation by methanogenic bacteria, mainly methane and carbon dioxide.
items.quote: Biogas dihasilkan dari fermentasi anaerobik bahan organik oleh bakteri metanogen.

items.question: Why is capturing methane from organic waste and burning it for energy considered good for the climate?
items.correct: Methane, which has a high warming potential, is turned into CO2 with a lower potential, while producing energy
wrong: Burning removes all the carbon, so no greenhouse gas is left
Methane is not a greenhouse gas, so burning is only useful as an energy source
Burning turns CO2 into methane, which is safer for the climate
items.explanation: The module calls landfill methane a strong greenhouse gas; burning it turns it into CO2, which has a lower warming potential.
items.quote: Menangkap dan membakarnya sebagai energi mengubah metana (potensi pemanasan tinggi) menjadi CO2 (potensi lebih rendah) sambil menghasilkan energi.

items.question: Food scraps thrown into a landfill rot without oxygen. Which gas forms, and how can its emissions be reduced?
items.correct: Methane; emissions are reduced by aerobic composting and biogas capture
wrong: Mercury; emissions are reduced by putting food scraps in the B3 group
Dioxin from rotting; emissions are reduced by burning food scraps
No gas forms because organic waste can break down
items.explanation: Organic waste rotting without oxygen produces methane; the module says aerobic composting and biogas capture reduce those emissions.
items.quote: Sampah organik yang membusuk tanpa oksigen di TPA menghasilkan metana, gas rumah kaca dengan potensi pemanasan sekitar 25-28 kali CO2.

items.question: Explain the difference between aerobic and anaerobic composting, including what each one produces.

rubricPoints.point: Aerobic composting uses microorganisms that need oxygen.
rubricPoints.quote: Mikroorganisme yang memerlukan oksigen mengurai bahan organik.

rubricPoints.point: Aerobic composting is faster, and its heat helps kill pathogens and weed seeds.
rubricPoints.quote: Prosesnya lebih cepat dan menghasilkan panas 50-70°C yang membantu membunuh patogen (kuman penyakit) dan biji gulma.

rubricPoints.point: The process without oxygen (anaerobic) produces biogas through fermentation by methanogenic bacteria.
rubricPoints.quote: Biogas dihasilkan dari fermentasi anaerobik bahan organik oleh bakteri metanogen.

items.question: Why should organic waste be turned into compost or biogas instead of being thrown into the landfill? Give reasons about its environmental impact.

rubricPoints.point: Organic waste rotting without oxygen in a landfill produces methane, a greenhouse gas.
rubricPoints.quote: Sampah organik yang membusuk tanpa oksigen di TPA menghasilkan metana, gas rumah kaca dengan potensi pemanasan sekitar 25-28 kali CO2.

rubricPoints.point: Recycling reduces the load on landfills and the negative impact of waste.
rubricPoints.quote: Daur ulang adalah bagian dari strategi pengelolaan sampah untuk mengurangi beban TPA (Tempat Pemrosesan Akhir) dan dampak negatif sampah terhadap lingkungan.

rubricPoints.point: Composting produces compost that is useful as organic fertiliser.
rubricPoints.quote: Pengomposan adalah proses dekomposisi bahan organik oleh mikroorganisme dalam kondisi terkontrol untuk menghasilkan kompos sebagai pupuk organik (Damanhuri dan Padmi, 2010).

items.question: Used paper and cardboard break down naturally. Which fibres are they made from?
items.correct: Plant fibres
wrong: Synthetic materials
Mineral materials
Plastic and aluminium layers
items.explanation: The module says paper and cardboard come from plant fibres, so they can break down.
items.quote: Kertas dan karton berasal dari serat tumbuhan sehingga dapat terurai, tetapi di sistem pemilahan sehari-hari sering ditaruh pada kelompok anorganik daur ulang karena lebih bernilai bila didaur ulang menjadi kertas baru (lihat Bab 4).

items.question: In everyday sorting, which group is used paper often put in, and why?
items.correct: Recyclable inorganic, because it is worth more when recycled into new paper
wrong: The B3 group, because paper ink is a hazardous and toxic material
The residual group, because paper cannot be recycled
The rubber and synthetic textile group
items.explanation: Paper is biodegradable, but in everyday sorting it is often put with recyclable inorganic waste because it is worth more recycled.
items.quote: Kertas berasal dari serat tumbuhan sehingga bersifat dapat terurai, namun dalam pemilahan sehari-hari sering dimasukkan ke anorganik daur ulang karena lebih bernilai didaur ulang menjadi kertas.

items.question: Why can paper only be recycled a few times?
items.correct: Its cellulose fibres get shorter every time it is recycled
wrong: Its ink cannot be removed after the first recycling
Paper must be melted at high temperatures like metal
Paper becomes non-biodegradable after being mixed with water
items.explanation: The module explains that cellulose fibres get shorter with each recycling, so paper can only be recycled about 5-7 times.
items.quote: Serat selulosa kertas memendek setiap kali didaur ulang, sehingga kertas dapat didaur ulang sekitar 5-7 kali (Arief, 2016).

items.question: In paper recycling, what happens in the de-inking stage?
items.correct: The ink is removed from the paper
wrong: The paper is melted into pellets
The paper is separated with a magnet
The paper is coated with plastic to make it last
items.explanation: In the module's paper recycling stages, de-inking is the stage where ink is removed; pellets and magnets are used for plastic and metal.
items.quote: 3. Penghilangan tinta (de-inking).

items.question: Plain cardboard and greasy paper from a fried-food wrapper are both made of paper. What is the difference when composting them?
items.correct: Greasy paper is not suitable for composting, while plain cardboard is an organic product that can break down
wrong: Greasy paper breaks down faster because the oil helps microbes
Both are B3 because they come from food packaging
Plain cardboard cannot break down because it is thick, while greasy paper can
items.explanation: The module lists plain cardboard as a biodegradable organic product, but plastic-coated, greasy or laminated paper is not suitable for composting.
items.quote: Kertas berlapis plastik, berminyak, atau berlaminasi (misalnya kemasan karton minuman, lihat 4.6) tidak cocok dikomposkan.

items.question: A student quotes a number of trees saved per tonne of recycled paper. What is the recommended attitude?
items.correct: Check that number against a primary source, because it varies between sources and between mills
wrong: Use the number straight away because every source gives the same number
Assume that recycling paper saves no raw material at all
Replace it with the aluminium energy saving figure because it applies to every material
items.explanation: The module says recycling paper saves raw material, water and energy, but the quoted savings vary and need to be checked.
items.quote: Besaran penghematan yang sering dikutip (misalnya jumlah pohon atau liter air per ton) bervariasi antar sumber dan antar pabrik, sehingga sebaiknya diverifikasi dari sumber primer sebelum dipakai sebagai data.

items.question: Explain where paper and cardboard sit in waste classification: their material properties and their group in sorting practice.

rubricPoints.point: Paper and cardboard come from plant fibres, so they can break down.
rubricPoints.quote: Kertas dan karton berasal dari serat tumbuhan sehingga dapat terurai, tetapi di sistem pemilahan sehari-hari sering ditaruh pada kelompok anorganik daur ulang karena lebih bernilai bila didaur ulang menjadi kertas baru (lihat Bab 4).

rubricPoints.point: In everyday sorting, paper is often put with recyclable inorganic waste because it is worth more recycled.
rubricPoints.quote: Kertas berasal dari serat tumbuhan sehingga bersifat dapat terurai, namun dalam pemilahan sehari-hari sering dimasukkan ke anorganik daur ulang karena lebih bernilai didaur ulang menjadi kertas.

rubricPoints.point: Plastic-coated, greasy or laminated paper is not suitable for composting.
rubricPoints.quote: Kertas berlapis plastik, berminyak, atau berlaminasi (misalnya kemasan karton minuman, lihat 4.6) tidak cocok dikomposkan.

items.question: Describe how used paper is made into new paper and why the number of times it can be recycled is limited.

rubricPoints.point: The fibres are broken down in water (pulping).
rubricPoints.quote: 2. Perendaman dan pelumatan serat dalam air (pulping).

rubricPoints.point: The ink is removed (de-inking) before the fibres are screened and formed again.
rubricPoints.quote: 3. Penghilangan tinta (de-inking).

rubricPoints.point: The cellulose fibres get shorter each time they are recycled, so the number of recycling rounds is limited.
rubricPoints.quote: Serat selulosa kertas memendek setiap kali didaur ulang, sehingga kertas dapat didaur ulang sekitar 5-7 kali (Arief, 2016).

items.question: Used plastic packaging is hard to break down in the environment. Which property of the material causes this?
items.correct: It comes from synthetic materials that are very hard for microorganisms to break down
wrong: It comes from living things
It contains hazardous materials, so it is always B3
It can be composted together with food scraps
items.explanation: The module says non-organic waste, including plastic, comes from synthetic or inorganic materials that are very hard for microorganisms to break down.
items.quote: Sampah non-organik berasal dari bahan sintetis atau bahan anorganis yang tidak dapat atau sangat sulit diuraikan mikroorganisme.

items.question: According to SIPSN 2024 data, where does plastic rank in Indonesia's national waste composition?
items.correct: Second, after food scraps
wrong: First, ahead of food scraps
Third, after wood and twigs
Last, after paper and cardboard
items.explanation: The Chapter 1 summary names food scraps as the largest component, followed by plastic.
items.quote: Di Indonesia 2024, sisa makanan adalah komponen terbesar (39,87%), disusul plastik (19,54%).

items.question: In plastic recycling, what is the resin identification code (1 = PET, 2 = HDPE, and so on) used for?
items.correct: To sort plastic at the collection stage
wrong: To set the temperature of a compost pile
To mark plastic as B3 waste
To separate plastic with a magnet
items.explanation: The first stage of plastic recycling in the module is collection and sorting by resin identification code.
items.quote: 1. Pengumpulan dan pemilahan berdasarkan kode jenis resin (1 = PET, 2 = HDPE, dan seterusnya).

items.question: PET and HDPE flakes are mixed in a water tank. Which plastic is taken from the water surface?
items.correct: HDPE, because its density is lower than water's
wrong: PET, because its density is lower than water's
PET, because its density is higher than water's
Neither, because both sink
items.explanation: The worked example in the module shows HDPE (0.95) floats and PET (1.38) sinks compared with water (1.00).
items.quote: Jawab: HDPE (0,95 < 1,00) mengapung dan diambil dari permukaan; PET (1,38 > 1,00) tenggelam dan diambil dari dasar.

items.question: PP and HDPE flakes both float in water. What is needed to separate them?
items.correct: A liquid with a density between 0.90 and 0.95 g/cm3, for example a mixture of alcohol and water
wrong: A magnet, because PP is attracted to magnets and HDPE is not
A liquid with a density above 1.38 g/cm3
A liquid with a density below 0.90 g/cm3
items.explanation: Because both are lighter than water, the module suggests a liquid with a density between those of PP and HDPE.
items.quote: Untuk memisahkan PP dari HDPE, diperlukan larutan dengan massa jenis antara 0,90 dan 0,95 g/cm3 (misalnya campuran alkohol dan air).

items.question: According to the 3R priority order, which action comes first for single-use plastic?
items.correct: Using less of it in the first place (reduce)
wrong: Recycling it straight away, because recycle comes before reduce
Using it again (reuse), because reuse comes before reduce
Burying it in the landfill so it does not spread in the environment
items.explanation: The module says the 3R order shows priority: reduce comes before reuse, and reuse comes before recycle.
items.quote: Urutan menunjukkan prioritas: Reduce lebih utama daripada Reuse, dan Reuse lebih utama daripada Recycle.

items.question: Explain the stages of plastic recycling, from collection to material for new products.

rubricPoints.point: Plastic is collected and sorted by resin identification code.
rubricPoints.quote: 1. Pengumpulan dan pemilahan berdasarkan kode jenis resin (1 = PET, 2 = HDPE, dan seterusnya).

rubricPoints.point: The plastic is cleaned and then shredded into flakes.
rubricPoints.quote: 3. Pencacahan (shredding) menjadi serpihan (flakes).

rubricPoints.point: The flakes are melted at a high temperature.
rubricPoints.quote: 4. Peleburan pada suhu tinggi (sekitar 200-300°C).

rubricPoints.point: The melt is formed into recycled plastic pellets.
rubricPoints.quote: 5. Pembentukan pelet plastik daur ulang.

items.question: Explain how the idea of density is used to separate types of plastic in recycling facilities, using PET and HDPE as examples.

rubricPoints.point: An object floats when its density is lower than the density of the fluid.
rubricPoints.quote: Benda mengapung dalam fluida bila massa jenisnya lebih kecil daripada massa jenis fluida.

rubricPoints.point: HDPE floats and PET sinks in water, so they can be collected separately.
rubricPoints.quote: Jawab: HDPE (0,95 < 1,00) mengapung dan diambil dari permukaan; PET (1,38 > 1,00) tenggelam dan diambil dari dasar.

rubricPoints.point: This sink-float separation is used in recycling facilities.
rubricPoints.quote: Kerapatan dipakai pada pemisahan apung-tenggelam (float-sink) di fasilitas daur ulang.

items.question: When sorting glass items, which group of items can be collected together?
items.correct: Glass bottles, broken window glass and mirrors
wrong: Fluorescent tubes and energy-saving lamps (CFL)
Aluminium cans and metal wire
Styrofoam and plastic bags
items.explanation: The module gives glass bottles, broken window glass and mirrors as examples of glass waste; fluorescent tubes and CFLs are B3.
items.quote: Botol kaca, pecahan kaca jendela dan cermin.

items.question: In glass recycling, how is glass waste sorted?
items.correct: By its colour
wrong: By its resin identification code
By its magnetic properties
By its moisture content
items.explanation: The module says glass is sorted by colour before it is washed, crushed, melted and formed again.
items.quote: Kaca: dipilah menurut warna, dicuci, dihancurkan (cullet), dilebur, dan dibentuk ulang.

items.question: Why are fluorescent tubes, neon lamps and CFLs not put with ordinary glass waste?
items.correct: Because they contain mercury, so they are B3 waste
wrong: Because they are made of plastic, not glass
Because they can be composted with organic waste
Because their glass is attracted to magnets
items.explanation: The module separates ordinary incandescent bulbs from fluorescent tubes, neon lamps and CFLs, which contain mercury and are therefore B3.
items.quote: Lampu bohlam pijar biasa terbuat dari kaca dan kawat logam, tetapi lampu TL, neon, dan lampu hemat energi (CFL) mengandung merkuri sehingga termasuk sampah B3 (Bab 2).

items.question: When waste is sorted with a magnet in a recycling facility, how does glass behave?
items.correct: It is not attracted to the magnet, just like aluminium and plastic
wrong: It is attracted to the magnet like iron and steel
It is attracted to the magnet if the glass is dark
It is attracted to the magnet if the glass is broken into cullet
items.explanation: The module says only ferromagnetic metals such as iron and steel are attracted to magnets; glass is not.
items.quote: Logam feromagnetik (besi, baja) tertarik magnet, sedangkan aluminium, tembaga, kaca, dan plastik tidak.

items.question: What is the difference between recycling glass and recycling paper?
items.correct: Glass can be recycled many times without losing quality, while paper fibres get shorter every time they are recycled
wrong: Paper can be recycled endlessly, while glass only once
Both lose quality and can only be recycled once
Both are processed by breaking them down in water (pulping)
items.explanation: The module says glass does not lose quality when recycled, while paper fibres get shorter, so paper can only be recycled a few times.
items.quote: Kaca dapat didaur ulang berkali-kali tanpa kehilangan mutu; botol utuh lebih baik dipakai ulang (reuse).

items.question: A CFL breaks in a bedroom. Which action is safe?
items.correct: Wearing gloves and collecting the pieces with stiff card or sticky tape
wrong: Sweeping up the pieces and throwing them in the ordinary glass group
Vacuuming the pieces so none are left behind
Burning the pieces so the mercury disappears
items.explanation: CFLs contain mercury; the module asks for the pieces to be collected with gloves, without a broom or vacuum cleaner, and treated as B3.
items.quote: Gunakan sarung tangan; kumpulkan pecahan dengan kertas karton atau selotip.

items.question: Explain the glass recycling process and why intact glass bottles are better reused.

rubricPoints.point: Glass is sorted by colour, washed, crushed into cullet, melted and formed again.
rubricPoints.quote: Kaca: dipilah menurut warna, dicuci, dihancurkan (cullet), dilebur, dan dibentuk ulang.

rubricPoints.point: Glass can be recycled many times without losing quality, but intact bottles are better reused.
rubricPoints.quote: Kaca dapat didaur ulang berkali-kali tanpa kehilangan mutu; botol utuh lebih baik dipakai ulang (reuse).

rubricPoints.point: In the 3Rs, reuse comes before recycle.
rubricPoints.quote: Urutan menunjukkan prioritas: Reduce lebih utama daripada Reuse, dan Reuse lebih utama daripada Recycle.

items.question: Explain why not every glass item may be put in the ordinary non-organic group.

rubricPoints.point: Fluorescent tubes, neon lamps and CFLs contain mercury, so they are B3.
rubricPoints.quote: Lampu bohlam pijar biasa terbuat dari kaca dan kawat logam, tetapi lampu TL, neon, dan lampu hemat energi (CFL) mengandung merkuri sehingga termasuk sampah B3 (Bab 2).

rubricPoints.point: Non-organic items such as glass move to the B3 group when they contain hazardous materials.
rubricPoints.quote: Sebagian benda non-organik (logam, kaca) sebenarnya berpindah ke kelompok B3 bila mengandung bahan berbahaya.

rubricPoints.point: Broken neon lamps or CFLs are kept in a closed container and treated as B3.
rubricPoints.quote: 3. Masukkan semua pecahan ke wadah tertutup (misalnya toples kaca bertutup) dan perlakukan sebagai sampah B3.

items.question: When sorting metal items, which group of items can be collected together?
items.correct: Aluminium drink cans, iron scraps and metal pipes
wrong: Glass bottles and mirrors
Plastic bags and styrofoam
Old tyres and rubber sandals
items.explanation: The module gives aluminium cans, iron scraps, steel, copper, pipes and metal wire as examples of metal waste.
items.quote: Kaleng aluminium minuman dan makanan kaleng, potongan besi, baja, tembaga, pipa dan kawat logam.

items.question: Roughly how much energy does recycling aluminium need compared with making it from bauxite ore?
items.correct: About 5%
wrong: About 50%
About 95%
The same, about 100%
items.explanation: The module says recycling aluminium needs only about 5% of the energy of producing it from bauxite; 95% is the saving.
items.quote: Daur ulang logam, khususnya aluminium, sangat hemat energi: mendaur ulang aluminium hanya memerlukan sekitar 5% energi dibanding membuatnya dari bijih bauksit (Tchobanoglous dkk., 1993).

items.question: What is a simple way to tell a steel can from an aluminium can?
items.correct: Hold a magnet near it: the can that sticks is steel
wrong: Hold a magnet near it: the can that sticks is aluminium
Read the resin identification code on the can
Sort the cans by colour, like sorting glass
items.explanation: The module explains that iron and steel are attracted to magnets while aluminium is not, so a magnet separates the two kinds of cans.
items.quote: Uji sederhana di kelas: dekatkan magnet ke kaleng; bila menempel, kaleng berbahan baja.

items.question: In the melting stage of metal recycling, which metal melts at a lower temperature?
items.correct: Aluminium, at about 660°C
wrong: Iron, at about 660°C
Aluminium, at about 1538°C
Both are the same, about 200-300°C
items.explanation: The module says aluminium is melted at about 660°C and iron at about 1538°C; 200-300°C is the melting temperature of plastic.
items.quote: 3. Peleburan di tanur: aluminium sekitar 660°C, besi sekitar 1538°C.

items.question: In theory, melting 1 kg of aluminium from 25°C needs about 0.97 MJ. Why does a real furnace need more energy?
items.correct: Because heat is lost; that calculation is only the minimum energy for melting
wrong: Because aluminium has to be heated to about 1538°C
Because the calculation already includes the energy for bauxite electrolysis
Because the latent heat of melting aluminium was left out
items.explanation: The module stresses that 0.97 MJ is the theoretical limit; real furnaces need more because of heat losses.
items.quote: Ini hanya energi minimum untuk meleburkan; tanur nyata memerlukan lebih banyak karena rugi panas.

items.question: What is the basis of the claim that recycling aluminium saves about 95% of the energy?
items.correct: The energy to melt aluminium is far smaller than the energy to produce it from bauxite by electrolysis
wrong: Used aluminium does not need to be melted when recycled
Aluminium melts at a higher temperature than iron
Aluminium cans can be separated with a magnet, so they do not need sorting
items.explanation: The module compares the theoretical energy for melting aluminium with the much larger energy for producing it from bauxite by electrolysis.
items.quote: Namun nilai ini jauh lebih kecil daripada energi untuk memproduksi aluminium dari bauksit lewat elektrolisis, yang menjadi dasar klaim bahwa daur ulang aluminium hemat sekitar 95% energi.

items.question: Explain the stages of metal recycling and how iron-based metals are separated from other metals.

rubricPoints.point: Metals are sorted by type; a magnet can separate iron-based metals.
rubricPoints.quote: 1. Pengumpulan dan pemilahan menurut jenis logam (magnet dapat memisahkan logam besi).

rubricPoints.point: The metal is cleaned of contaminants such as paint and plastic.
rubricPoints.quote: 2. Pembersihan dari kontaminan (cat, plastik).

rubricPoints.point: The metal is melted, refined, and then cast into ingots or new products.
rubricPoints.quote: 5. Pencetakan menjadi ingot atau produk baru.

rubricPoints.point: Iron and steel are attracted to magnets, while aluminium is not.
rubricPoints.quote: Logam feromagnetik (besi, baja) tertarik magnet, sedangkan aluminium, tembaga, kaca, dan plastik tidak.

items.question: Explain why recycling aluminium is strongly recommended, comparing the energy of recycling with producing it from ore.

rubricPoints.point: Recycling aluminium needs only about 5% of the energy of producing it from bauxite.
rubricPoints.quote: Daur ulang logam, khususnya aluminium, sangat hemat energi: mendaur ulang aluminium hanya memerlukan sekitar 5% energi dibanding membuatnya dari bijih bauksit (Tchobanoglous dkk., 1993).

rubricPoints.point: The theoretical energy to melt 1 kg of aluminium is about 0.97 MJ.
That energy is far smaller than producing it from bauxite by electrolysis, even though real furnaces need more because of heat losses.
rubricPoints.quote: Namun nilai ini jauh lebih kecil daripada energi untuk memproduksi aluminium dari bauksit lewat elektrolisis, yang menjadi dasar klaim bahwa daur ulang aluminium hemat sekitar 95% energi.

items.question: What kind of packaging is a drink carton such as a milk or juice box?
items.correct: Multilayer packaging
wrong: Metal packaging without layers
Plain paper packaging without layers
Glass packaging
items.explanation: The module calls drink cartons multilayer packaging.
items.quote: Kemasan karton minuman, misalnya kotak susu atau jus (sering dikenal dengan merek Tetra Pak), adalah kemasan berlapis (multilayer).

items.question: Which materials make up a drink carton?
items.correct: Paperboard coated with plastic and a thin layer of aluminium foil
wrong: Paperboard coated with glass
Plastic and steel
Plain paper only
items.explanation: The module says this packaging is mostly paperboard, coated with plastic and thin aluminium foil.
items.quote: Sebagian besar terdiri dari kertas karton, dilapisi plastik dan lapisan tipis aluminium foil.

items.question: Why is a used drink carton put with recyclable non-organic waste rather than compost?
items.correct: Its plastic and aluminium layers mean the packaging cannot be composted
wrong: Its paper contains mercury
The packaging is B3 waste
Its paper cannot be recycled at all
items.explanation: Even though it is mostly paper, this packaging has plastic and aluminium layers, so it cannot be composted and goes with recyclable non-organic waste.
items.quote: Kemasan karton minuman bekas termasuk sampah non-organik yang dapat didaur ulang meskipun sebagian besar bahannya kertas, karena berlapis plastik dan aluminium sehingga tidak dapat dikomposkan.

items.question: What do the plastic and aluminium layers in a drink carton do?
items.correct: They keep the drink fresh and stop leaks
wrong: They make the packaging easy to compost
They make the packaging stick to a magnet when sorted
They make the packaging B3 waste
items.explanation: The module says the plastic and aluminium layers keep the drink fresh and stop leaks.
items.quote: Lapisan plastik dan aluminium menjaga isi minuman tetap awet dan tidak bocor.

items.question: What happens in the pulping stage of drink carton recycling?
items.correct: The carton is mixed with water in a pulper so the paper fibres come away from the plastic and aluminium layers
wrong: The packaging is melted at about 660°C to separate the aluminium
The packaging is separated with a magnet to take out the aluminium
The packaging is composted so its plastic layer breaks down
items.explanation: According to the recycling stages quoted in the module, pulping uses water in a pulper to free the fibres from the plastic and aluminium.
items.quote: 2. Pulping: karton dicampur dengan air di mesin pulper sehingga serat kertas terlepas dari lapisan plastik dan aluminium.

items.question: After the paper fibres are separated, what happens to the PolyAl (the leftover plastic and aluminium)?
items.correct: It is shredded and processed into granules, then made into things such as corrugated roofing sheets
wrong: It is sent to the landfill because it cannot be processed
It is composted together with organic waste
It is handed to a B3 management facility
items.explanation: The module says PolyAl is shredded and processed into granules, and its products include corrugated roofing sheets.
items.quote: 4. Daur ulang PolyAl: plastik dan aluminium yang tersisa dicacah dan diolah menjadi granul.

items.question: Explain why drink cartons are treated differently from plain paper in waste sorting.

rubricPoints.point: This packaging has layers: paperboard, plastic and aluminium foil.
rubricPoints.quote: Sebagian besar terdiri dari kertas karton, dilapisi plastik dan lapisan tipis aluminium foil.

rubricPoints.point: Because it is layered, the packaging cannot be composted and goes with recyclable non-organic waste.
rubricPoints.quote: Kemasan karton minuman bekas termasuk sampah non-organik yang dapat didaur ulang meskipun sebagian besar bahannya kertas, karena berlapis plastik dan aluminium sehingga tidak dapat dikomposkan.

rubricPoints.point: Laminated paper such as drink cartons is not suitable for composting.
rubricPoints.quote: Kertas berlapis plastik, berminyak, atau berlaminasi (misalnya kemasan karton minuman, lihat 4.6) tidak cocok dikomposkan.

items.question: Describe how drink cartons are recycled in a facility that separates the fibres from the PolyAl layer.

rubricPoints.point: Pulping frees the paper fibres from the plastic and aluminium layers.
rubricPoints.quote: 2. Pulping: karton dicampur dengan air di mesin pulper sehingga serat kertas terlepas dari lapisan plastik dan aluminium.

rubricPoints.point: The fibres are cleaned, dried and then made into new paper sheets.
rubricPoints.quote: 3. Daur ulang serat: serat dibersihkan, diperas, dikeringkan, lalu dibuat menjadi lembaran kertas baru.

rubricPoints.point: The PolyAl is shredded and processed into granules.
rubricPoints.quote: 4. Daur ulang PolyAl: plastik dan aluminium yang tersisa dicacah dan diolah menjadi granul.

rubricPoints.point: The final products include paper products and corrugated roofing sheets.
rubricPoints.quote: 5. Produk: serat kertas menjadi produk kertas; PolyAl menjadi antara lain lembar atap gelombang.

items.question: Broken electronics contain metals that can be recovered. Why must they still be kept apart from ordinary metal waste?
items.correct: Because they also contain hazardous materials, so they are treated as B3 waste
wrong: Because they can be composted
Because they contain no recoverable metals
Because they are paper waste
items.explanation: The module says e-waste contains metals but also hazardous materials, so it is treated as B3 waste.
items.quote: Perangkat elektronik rusak (e-waste) mengandung logam, tetapi juga mengandung bahan berbahaya sehingga dibahas sebagai sampah B3 di Bab 2.

items.question: How many groups are used in good waste sorting at the source?
items.correct: Three: organic, non-organic and B3
wrong: Two: organic and non-organic
Four: organic, plastic, paper and metal
One: all waste is mixed and then sorted at the landfill
items.explanation: The module stresses that good sorting at the source uses three groups, with B3 as the third group.
items.quote: Pemilahan di sumber yang baik memakai tiga kelompok, bukan dua.

items.question: What is the community's role in managing e-waste?
items.correct: Sorting it, storing it safely and handing it in at a collection point
wrong: Taking it apart and melting it themselves to get the metals
Burning the cables so the copper is easy to take
Throwing it away with ordinary metal waste
items.explanation: The module says recovering materials from B3 may only be done by licensed facilities; the community sorts, stores and hands it in.
items.quote: Peran masyarakat adalah memilah, menyimpan aman, dan menyetor.

items.question: What happens if B3 such as broken electronics ends up in the landfill with ordinary waste?
items.correct: Leachate can carry heavy metals into the soil and groundwater
wrong: The electronics break down into compost
The electronics produce biogas that is worth energy
Their heavy metals turn into harmless methane
items.explanation: The module explains that B3 piling up in the landfill is carried by leachate, so heavy metals pollute the soil and groundwater.
items.quote: B3 yang terbuang bersama sampah biasa menumpuk di TPA, lalu lindi (cairan rembesan) membawa logam berat ke tanah dan air tanah.

items.question: Someone burns old cables and soaks circuit boards in acid to get the metals out. Why is this dangerous?
items.correct: It is very dangerous for workers and the environment; B3 recycling may only be done by licensed facilities
wrong: It is recommended because it counts as recycle in the 3R principle
It is safe as long as it is done outdoors
It is fine because metals from e-waste are not dangerous
items.explanation: The module warns that informal e-waste recycling is very dangerous and may only be done by licensed facilities.
items.quote: Daur ulang e-waste secara informal (membakar kabel, merendam papan sirkuit dengan asam) sangat berbahaya bagi pekerja dan lingkungan.

items.question: Substances such as mercury and lead from B3 can biomagnify. What does that mean?
items.correct: Their concentration rises at each level of the food chain
wrong: Their concentration falls at each level of the food chain
Microorganisms break them down into compost
They turn into methane in the landfill
items.explanation: The module explains biomagnification as the concentration of a substance rising at each level of the food chain.
items.quote: Zat seperti merkuri dan timbal terakumulasi di tubuh makhluk hidup dan terbiomagnifikasi (konsentrasi naik di setiap tingkat rantai makanan).

items.question: Explain the safe steps for handling e-waste or used batteries at home until they are handed to the right place.

rubricPoints.point: Recognise B3 from its label and hazard symbols.
rubricPoints.quote: 1. Kenali: baca label produk; simbol bahaya (api, tengkorak, korosif, tanda seru) menandakan B3.

rubricPoints.point: Keep it apart in a special container that is dry, closed and away from children and heat.
rubricPoints.quote: 2. Pisahkan: sediakan satu wadah khusus B3 yang kering, tertutup, dan jauh dari anak-anak serta panas.

rubricPoints.point: Do not burn batteries or electronic waste.
rubricPoints.quote: Jangan membakar baterai, aerosol, atau sampah elektronik.

rubricPoints.point: Hand it in at a collection point, for example an e-waste drop box or a manufacturer take-back programme.
rubricPoints.quote: 4. Kumpulkan sedikit demi sedikit, lalu serahkan ke titik pengumpulan: dinas lingkungan hidup, bank sampah yang menerima B3 atau e-waste, drop box e-waste, program take-back produsen, atau pengelola limbah B3 berizin.

items.question: Why is e-waste not recycled by people themselves, even though it contains valuable metals? Also explain the impact if it is thrown away or processed carelessly.

rubricPoints.point: B3 waste is not recycled by people themselves.
rubricPoints.quote: Berbeda dari plastik atau kertas, sampah B3 tidak didaur ulang oleh masyarakat sendiri.

rubricPoints.point: Recovering materials from B3 may only be done by licensed facilities.
rubricPoints.quote: Pemulihan material dari B3 hanya boleh dilakukan fasilitas berizin.

rubricPoints.point: Informal recycling is very dangerous for workers and the environment.
rubricPoints.quote: Daur ulang e-waste secara informal (membakar kabel, merendam papan sirkuit dengan asam) sangat berbahaya bagi pekerja dan lingkungan.

rubricPoints.point: B3 thrown into the landfill is carried by leachate into the soil and groundwater.
rubricPoints.quote: B3 yang terbuang bersama sampah biasa menumpuk di TPA, lalu lindi (cairan rembesan) membawa logam berat ke tanah dan air tanah.
